title: The inclusion-exclusion principle
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point is about social inclusion and exclusion in a Society and Culture course, which is a different idea from the inclusion-exclusion counting principle in Specialist Mathematics.

draft.title: The inclusion-exclusion principle
card: To count items in A or B (or both), add the count of A and the count of B. Then subtract the count of items in both.
In symbols: |A or B| = |A| + |B| − |A and B|. Items in both were counted twice, so one count is taken away.
Example: of 30 students, 18 play netball, 12 swim and 5 do both. Students doing at least one: 18 + 12 − 5 = 25.
Sometimes the overlap must be worked out. Whole numbers divisible by both 2 and 3 are the multiples of 6.
draft.remember: Add the two groups, then subtract the overlap once so nothing is counted twice.

a.q: In a year group of 40, 24 study French, 15 study Italian and 6 study both. How many study French or Italian?
a.why: 24 + 15 − 6 = 33. Adding only 24 + 15 = 39 counts the 6 students in both subjects twice.
a.clue: Students in both subjects appear in both counts.

b.q: How many whole numbers from 1 to 50 are divisible by 3 or by 5?
b.why: There are 16 multiples of 3, 10 multiples of 5 and 3 multiples of 15, so 16 + 10 − 3 = 23. The option 26 adds without taking away the overlap.
b.clue: A number divisible by both 3 and 5 is a multiple of 15.
